haiku-low.q1: The connection returns, the app comes to the foreground, and every 60 seconds while online.
haiku-low.q3: The server detects it by comparing the change's base_version with the note's current version; a mismatch is a conflict.
haiku-low.q4: Note N keeps the first-accepted text at version 4; the second phone's text is saved as a separate '<title> (conflict)' note.
haiku-low.q5: One change: the latest full body with the original base_version, since repeated edits merge into the queued change.
haiku-low.q6: Each change has a UUID change_id; the server stores each result in processed_changes and returns it on retry without reapplying.
haiku-low.q7: In the phone's SQLite cursor, holding the highest applied seq; it is updated in the same transaction that applies a download page.
haiku-low.q8: The cursor did not move, so the next sync requests the same range again; no entries are skipped and reapplying is harmless.
haiku-low.q9: The upload result reports the conflict and the copy's id; then downloaded log entries set the note to the server's body, since nothing is pending.
haiku-low.q10: Only after the phone has read the server's result for that change.
haiku-low.q11: The phone keeps showing its local body; the pending change is resolved later through the upload rules.
haiku-low.q12: A new change, since the sent one is frozen. Its base_version follows the earlier result: returned version if accepted, old one if conflict.

sonnet.q1: The connection returning, the app coming to the foreground, and every 60 seconds while online.
sonnet.q3: The server. It compares the change's base_version to the note's current version; if equal it is accepted, otherwise it is a conflict.
sonnet.q4: The first write to arrive is accepted: note N holds that phone's body at version 4. The other phone's text is saved as a new note "<title> (conflict)" at version 1. Nothing is lost, and the server records both results in processed_changes.
sonnet.q5: One merged change with the latest body and the original base_version (a single change_id, full body, no diffs).
sonnet.q6: Each change has a change_id made once at creation and resent unchanged. The server checks processed_changes first. If the id is there, it returns the stored result and does nothing else.
sonnet.q7: In the phone's SQLite cursor table, which holds the highest server seq applied. It is updated only in the same SQLite transaction that applies a downloaded page, moving to that page's last seq.
sonnet.q8: The cursor stays where it was, because it moves only with a successful apply. The next sync asks again for entries after the same cursor, so none are skipped. Re-applying entries is harmless due to the version check.
sonnet.q9: The server's upload response says "conflict" with the conflict note's id. The phone removes the change from its outbox. Its download then brings the log entries for the winning version of N and the conflict copy N2, so N shows the winner's text and N2 holds its own text.
sonnet.q10: Only after the phone has read the server's result (accepted or conflict) for that change.
sonnet.q11: If the note has a pending change in the outbox, the phone does not overwrite the body. The UI keeps showing the local body, and the pending change resolves through the upload rules. NOT STATED on whether the version number is updated or whether the entry is retained for later.
sonnet.q12: It starts a new change. If the earlier change is accepted, the new change's base_version is set to the version the server returned. If the earlier one was a conflict, the new change keeps its old base_version and will conflict too. The sent change stays frozen.
